overview.headline: How the electoral college process elects the president and counts votes

keyPoints.point: Students learn the electoral college is a process established as a compromise between congressional and popular election.
keyPoints.quote: The Electoral College is a process, not a place.

keyPoints.point: The college consists of 538 electors and requires a majority of 270 electoral votes to elect the president.
keyPoints.quote: The Electoral College consists of 538 electors.

keyPoints.point: Most states use winner take all to award electors while Maine and Nebraska use a proportional system.
keyPoints.quote: Most States have a “winner-take-all” system that awards all electors to the Presidential candidate who wins the State's popular vote.

keyPoints.point: Electoral votes are counted in a joint session of congress on January 6 and the president is sworn in on January 20.
keyPoints.quote: Each State’s electoral votes are counted in a joint session of Congress on the 6th of January in the year following the meeting of the electors.

keyTerms.gloss: appointed individuals who cast electoral votes for president and vice president in their state
keyTerms.quote: The Electoral College consists of 538 electors.

keyTerms.gloss: group of electors linked to one presidential candidate and chosen by the party
keyTerms.quote: Each candidate running for President in your State has their own group of electors (known as a slate).

keyTerms.gloss: document prepared by the state executive listing appointed electors and votes received
keyTerms.quote: your State's Executive prepares a Certificate of Ascertainment listing the names of all the individuals on the slates for each candidate.

keyTerms.gloss: system that awards all of a state's electors to the candidate who wins the popular vote
keyTerms.quote: Most States have a “winner-take-all” system that awards all electors to the Presidential candidate who wins the State's popular vote.

keyTerms.gloss: elected members in a state's congressional delegation serving in the house and senate
keyTerms.quote: Your State has the same number of electors as it does Members in its Congressional delegation
